facilities.name: Falcon 9 first-stage test stand (current, 'big stand')
facilities.function: Static fires of every Falcon 9 / Falcon Heavy first stage (9 Merlin 1D). Partially underground, built 2014-2015 for F9 Full Thrust, in use since late 2015; single-core configuration.

footprint.flame_trench: triangular concrete flame trench / deflector opening SOUTH from the deck: ~75 m long (y -578 to -652), ~18 m wide at the stand widening to ~65 m at the mouth (x -185..-105 at the south end)

facilities.height_how_known: stand deck is near grade (partially underground stand, no tall tower over it in StratMap Jan 2020); a Falcon 9 booster standing in it rises ~41-47 m (stage + interstage). Kenny's photo also shows a blue lattice access tower beside it c. 2015-2017 (not standing in Jan 2020)
facilities.look: Concrete deck over a sloped, concrete-lined triangular exhaust trench (dark grey, scorched) that opens south; tall blue steel lattice access tower; white propellant/pressurant tanks and blue/grey pipe racks to the north and east; red crawler crane often parked beside it (2020-2021). From the south (Kenny's photo) you see the open trench mouth with the water tower to the left and the tripod to the right.
facilities.notes: Kenny's aerial_test_stands.jpg looks NNE at this stand: pit in the centre, water tower left, tripod right.

facilities.name: The 'Tripod' (Beal Aerospace stand) - former F9 first-stage stand, now Raptor vertical stand
facilities.function: Built by Beal Aerospace c. 1999-2000 (the '220-feet tall vertical-fire stand ... for larger engines' of Beal's 1999 release). SpaceX added a tall access tower with retractable floors on top and a water-cooled flame diverter at its base; F9 first-stage firings 2008 to mid-2015 (last: Jason-3 stage). Idle 2015-2019; from Oct 2019 converted to a vertical Raptor test stand (tower removed and laid down), in use for Raptor since ~2020.
facilities.height_how_known: shadow length on StratMap Jan 2020 (~82 m, sun elevation 39+-2 deg from date + container-shadow calibration) -> ~66 m incl. the structure on top; matches Beal's 1999 '220-feet tall vertical-fire stand' (67 m). Concrete legs alone are lower (~40 m, estimate)
facilities.look: Three massive grey concrete legs (a tripod) carrying a concrete ring/deck; 2008-2019 a tall blue steel lattice access tower on top (white F9 stage inside); today blue steel platforms and handrails on the deck, scaffolding, a white clad building beside it (to the east). Exhaust goes down between the legs into a flame diverter.
facilities.notes: Kenny's aerial_test_stands.jpg: the right-hand structure with the blue tower on three concrete legs and a dark pit below.

facilities.name: Falcon 9 structural test stand
facilities.function: Structural/pressure testing of tanks and stage sections.
facilities.height_how_known: shadow on StratMap Jan 2020: ~74 m long north of the stand -> ~60 m (+-10%); its lattice shadow is the long one crossing the loop road north of the stands
facilities.look: Tall dark steel lattice tower with stair/platform levels, beside rows of horizontal white tanks just north of the tripod; long thin lattice shadow.

facilities.name: Central water tower (stands area)
facilities.function: Elevated water storage feeding the stand deluge/cooling water.

footprint.how_known: StratMap Jan 2020: tank ~16 m across (shadow width), legs spread ~22 m (OSM ring 23 m)

facilities.height_how_known: two independent estimates: (1) StratMap Jan 2020 shadow, base -> tank-shadow centre ~94 m at sun elevation 39+-2 deg -> tank centre ~75 m (68-82); (2) Kenny's aerial_test_stands.jpg proportions, height ~5.5x tank diameter -> ~85 m. Use ~75 m to tank centre, ~83 m to top
facilities.look: Very tall white multi-leg lattice water tower (legs + X bracing, white) with a white near-spherical tank (~16 m) on top: the tallest thing in the central stands area; next to two white ground tanks on a grassy round mound inside the loop road.

facilities.name: Ground water storage tanks by the central water tower
facilities.function: Ground water storage for the stand deluge (two white flat-bottom tanks).
facilities.height_how_known: estimate from shadows (low walls, domed roofs)
facilities.look: White cylindrical tanks with shallow domed roofs on a grassy round mound inside the loop road.

facilities.name: Central stands tank farm (LOX / RP-1 / LN2 / helium)
facilities.function: Propellant and pressurant storage for the tripod and first-stage stand: rows of horizontal white tanks, vertical helium bottles (OSM content=helium), small vertical tanks.

footprint.how_known: OSM tank rings (horizontal tanks show as large overlapping 'r' values)

facilities.look: Long white horizontal cylinders on saddles in parallel rows, silver vertical tanks, pipe racks.

facilities.name: Stands-area hangar / shop
facilities.function: Hangar/workshop serving the central stands (labelled 'HANGAR' on the 2015 aerial).
facilities.look: Long light-grey metal building with a low gabled roof, cars parked along its east side.

facilities.name: Raptor test complex (north): horizontal test bays
facilities.function: Original Raptor horizontal test stands (first Raptor firing Sept 2016; second horizontal stand completed 2019); multiple bays firing roughly north into scoured exhaust fans; sea-level and vacuum Raptors.

footprint.how_known: OSM ring (stand) + works polygon 910751658 (whole complex inside the oval road, ~87,700 m2)

facilities.height_how_known: estimate (test-cell structures 10-20 m; tallest frames ~25 m)
facilities.look: Concrete test cells (walls, roofs, yellow jib cranes, dense silver pipework, black steel frames) clustered at the north end of a caliche pad; 2-4 exhaust troughs (light concrete wedges) fan NNW/N/NNE into bare scoured earth 100-200 m long; a grey flat-roof shop (~27 x 25 m) south-east of the cells; a long white pipe rack runs east at y~370 toward the propellant farm. The pad sits inside an oval caliche loop road with an earth berm on its north side.

facilities.name: Raptor vertical test stand (2021)
facilities.function: Vertical sea-level Raptor stand built Jan-May 2021 ('New Raptor Stand'), up to 1-2 firings/day; flame trench opens south.

footprint.flame_trench: triangular trench opening south, OSM ring 926002317

facilities.height_how_known: estimate from NSF 2021 photo (stand top a little above the white vertical tanks)
facilities.look: Steel stand over a concrete triangular flame trench like a small version of the F9 stand; white vertical tanks beside it.

facilities.name: Raptor complex shop building
facilities.function: Grey flat-roofed shop/hangar on the Raptor pad (engine handling).
facilities.look: Light-grey metal building with a flat/low roof and roll-up doors.

facilities.name: Raptor propellant tank farm along the north road
facilities.function: LOX / methane / LN2 storage feeding the north Raptor complex by an east-west pipe rack.

footprint.how_known: OSM tank rings along the N-S road x~400-417, y 239-450

facilities.look: Rows of white tanks beside the road; a long pipe rack runs west ~500 m to the Raptor complex at y~365.

facilities.name: Raptor North test stand (new, 2025)
facilities.function: New horizontal Raptor stand with several bays; first firings mid-2025 (2 s, then 19 s in Aug 2025); Raptor 3.

footprint.flame_trench: long concrete exhaust trench/apron to the WEST of the stand, ~77 m long, ~8 m wide at the stand widening to ~25 m

facilities.look: Black steel test-cell block with pipe racks, white horizontal tanks (~40 m long) east of it, white vertical tanks, bright caliche pad.

facilities.name: Raptor South test stand (new, 2025)
facilities.function: New Raptor stand used for Raptor 3 development (record burns 152-201 s in Aug 2025, 354 s later).

footprint.flame_trench: exhaust trench to the WEST, ~76 m long, ~24 m wide at the outer end

facilities.look: Twin of the North stand: black steel cell, horizontal and vertical white tanks to the east, N-S pipe rack linking it to the North stand (x~905).

facilities.name: Vertical second-stage test stand ('new test site', S2 stand)
facilities.function: Falcon 9 second-stage (MVac) static fires; flame trench dug 2015, work resumed late 2017, nearing completion Oct 2019; similar design to the newer first-stage stand.

footprint.flame_trench: concrete trench opening SOUTH, ~50 m long, ~8 m wide at the stand to ~31 m at the mouth (StratMap 2020); Esri 2025 shows the opening ~80 m long incl. the scoured run-out
footprint.apron: large dark paved apron NORTH of the stand, ~100 x 80 m (Esri 2025)

facilities.height_how_known: estimate (elevated deck + mount ring; F9 second stage ~14 m stands on it)
facilities.look: Open sloped concrete flame trench with an elevated steel deck and mount ring over its head, flanked by two flat-roofed concrete buildings; grey metal sheds; white water tank nearby.

facilities.name: East water tower (by the S2 stand)
facilities.function: Water storage near the new stage-2 stand (possibly the 250,000 gal elevated / 500,000 gal ground tanks of the 2019 Walker Partners water-system project).
facilities.height_how_known: estimate: typical 250,000 gal elevated tank (Walker Partners 2019 water-system project) 40-45 m; shadow not measurable in the crops
facilities.look: White steel near-spherical tank on a white lattice leg tower (smaller than the central one); a white ground storage tank (~12 m) just north at (1049,-629).

facilities.name: Propellant compounds east of the Merlin stands (S2 stand feed)
facilities.function: Three fenced compounds of tall vertical white tanks along the road between the Merlin complex and the S2 stand, plus a compound with horizontal tanks at (535,-815); feed the S2 stand via a long pipe rack.
facilities.height_how_known: shadow ~17 m on StratMap -> ~14 m vertical tanks
facilities.look: Gravel compounds with chain-link fence, 3-5 tall white vertical tanks each, process skids, small white buildings; black pipe rack on low supports to the east.

facilities.name: Merlin engine dual test stand (vertical M1D stands)
facilities.function: Acceptance firings of Merlin 1D engines, two vertical cells; 'VERTICAL M1D TEST STANDS' on the 2015 aerial.
facilities.height_how_known: rough shadow estimate on StratMap Jan 2020 (~35 m shadow)
facilities.look: Cluster of tall steel test towers (grey/blue framing, white tanks, pipework) at the south end of a long tank row; a huge dark scorched concrete exhaust apron/fan (~60 x 120 m) on its east side; burn scar spreading east-south-east on the grass.

facilities.name: Upper-stage test stand (older vertical stage-2 / MVac stand)
facilities.function: Falcon 9 second-stage firings before the new S2 stand; 'VERTICAL STAGE 2 TEST STAND' on the 2015 aerial; next to the M1D stands.
facilities.look: Tall enclosed steel tower with tanks, part of the M1D/stage-2 complex.

facilities.name: MVac test stand
facilities.function: Merlin Vacuum engine firings (OSM name).
facilities.look: Steel stand south of the dual stand.

facilities.name: Horizontal M1D test stand (probable) / north Merlin cell
facilities.function: Compact stand with buildings and tanks north of the vertical Merlin stands, by a small pond; probably the 'HORIZONTAL M1D TEST STAND' (#12) of the 2015 numbered aerial.
facilities.look: Fenced compound with a white building, steel test frame, horizontal and vertical tanks, pipe bridge to the main tank row; small dark pond to the east.

facilities.name: Merlin / stage-2 complex tank farm
facilities.function: Propellant storage for the M1D / upper-stage / MVac stands: line of small tanks along the road north of the complex, large tanks at its south end.
facilities.look: White horizontal and vertical tanks; a big round black-topped tank at (506,-1335) (visible in the 2008 aerial as a black disc); long dark lined pond/trench east of the stands (x 538-592, y -1382..-1441).

facilities.name: Round dark-topped tank by the Merlin stands
facilities.function: Large round tank or basin with a dark top/water surface (visible as a black disc since 2008); probably water for deluge/cooling.
facilities.look: Concrete/steel ring wall, black interior (water or black roof), white tanks around it.

facilities.name: Lined retention basin east of the Merlin stands
facilities.function: Two-cell concrete-walled, black-lined water retention basin at the foot of the Merlin exhaust apron.
facilities.look: Black liner water in concrete-walled rectangular cells, white curbs.

facilities.name: Blockhouse / control room
facilities.function: Test control (the 'engine test bunker'); 'BLOCKHOUSE/CONTROL' on the 2015 aerials; OSM 'Control Room'.
facilities.look: Low flat-roofed concrete building with an attached dark-roofed wing, small parking lot to its south-west; 2012 interior photo shows a windowless control room with consoles (Jurvetson).

facilities.name: Site offices, shops and old core-storage hangar ('Central Site')
facilities.function: Main office/shop building (OSM 'SpaceX Central Shop'), connected office wing and the large white hangar at its south-east end ('OLD CORE STORAGE HANGAR' on the 2015 aerial); main parking lot to the west.
facilities.height_how_known: estimate: single storey shop bays ~8-9 m to ridge; 2-storey office addition with observation deck built 2013-2014 (TDLR EABPRJB4802760)
facilities.look: White/light-grey corrugated metal buildings with blue trim and low gabled roofs; a dark-grey single-storey office wing with a glass entrance canopy and flagpoles; the hangar has a full-height sliding door on its east end; landscaped strip and big asphalt lot.

facilities.name: Old core-storage hangar (big white hangar at the offices)
facilities.function: Large hangar at the SE end of the office/shop complex ('OLD CORE STORAGE HANGAR' on the 2015 aerial): horizontal stage storage and work.
facilities.height_how_known: estimate from the 2013 CC0 aerial (door height vs. pickups)
facilities.look: White ribbed metal hangar with blue trim and a low gabled roof; full-height sliding hangar door with a blue rail on its east gable; HVAC units along the north wall.

facilities.name: Office/shop annex buildings north of the main lot
facilities.function: Grey gabled shop (OSM 233581958) and a white shed north-west of the main building.
facilities.look: Light-grey gabled metal building ~29 x 22 m; small white metal sheds; gravel yard.

facilities.name: Main parking lot
facilities.function: Staff parking west of the offices (~300+ spaces).
facilities.look: Asphalt with white striping, landscaped median with gravel and small trees.

facilities.name: Main entrance (office access drive off the south road)
facilities.function: No gatehouse is visible on the 2020/2022/2025 imagery. The concrete office drive leaves the east-west south road at about (105,-2003) and curves north (x~60-80) to the office junction at (100,-1715). The south road (concrete/asphalt with a yellow centre line) runs east to x~812 and on (asphalt) to a north-south road at x~1800-1950 that meets FM 2671 at about (1950,-2275): most likely the public approach ('1 Rocket Road').
facilities.look: Concrete two-lane drive with grass verges and white culvert headwalls; the site address is 1 Rocket Road, McGregor TX 76657.

facilities.name: Boneyard / scrap yard
facilities.function: Outdoor storage of hardware and debris ('BONE YARD: F9R-DEV1 DEBRIS' on the 2015 labelled aerial). In Aug 2025 NSF counted 40-50 retired Raptors rusting in a 'junkyard' area (location not stated; may be here or near the Raptor complex).
facilities.look: Gravel yard with rows of steel frames, stacked pipes, rusty parts and long lattice sections on the ground.

facilities.name: 'New core storage hangar' (2015 label) - long white hangar south of the boneyard
facilities.function: Stage storage hangar (under construction on the 2015 labelled aerial). Identification by position relative to the boneyard and the structural stand: medium.
facilities.look: Long white metal hangar with a dark steel-framed section at one end (2015), parking in front.

facilities.name: Dragon processing / deconstruction + early SuperDraco stand ('Dragon site')
facilities.function: Post-flight Dragon defueling and disassembly; labelled 'DRAGON DECONSTRUCTION, SUPERDRACO TEST STAND' (2015 labelled aerial) and '9 SUPERDRACO TEST STANDS' (2015 numbered aerial). In 2025 small bunkered test pads line the road to its north-west (see small_test_pads).

footprint.how_known: StratMap 2020: cluster of white metal buildings ~110 x 70 m

facilities.look: Cluster of white gabled metal buildings, one long white hall to the east, blue-roofed annex, process equipment between them.
facilities.notes: SuperDraco firing photos (2012, 2014) are attached because the 2015 aerials label this site as the SuperDraco test stand; which stand those photos show is not stated.

facilities.name: Small component test pads (north-west of the Dragon site)
facilities.function: Small concrete pads with test hardware along the road NW of the Dragon site (Esri 2025); probably the component / COPV / tank 'torture test' pads NSF mentions (2025).
facilities.look: Small round/square concrete pads with a box structure, gravel aprons.

facilities.name: SuperDraco test stand (west, OSM)
facilities.function: SuperDraco and Draco thruster firings (OSM 'Super Draco test stand').
facilities.look: Compact pad with dark-blue steel test cells, white sheds, a row of horizontal white tanks to the south, small red lattice frame.
facilities.notes: The DragonFly tethered SuperDraco hover test (Nov 2015, crane + blast wall) was at McGregor; its exact spot on the site is not identified.

facilities.name: Grasshopper / F9R-Dev1 launch site (west-south-west)
facilities.function: Half-acre concrete pad for Grasshopper (8 flights 2012-2013) and F9R-Dev1 (5 flights 2014, lost 22 Aug 2014); later a test stand with a lattice tower and tanks was added beside it.

footprint.pad: square concrete pad ~45 x 40 m centred about (-763,-1775) (half-acre per Wikipedia)
footprint.stand: later test stand with a dark lattice tower and tank farm at about (-690,-1700)
footprint.how_known: StratMap 2020 + 2013 CC0 aerial of the Grasshopper site

facilities.height_how_known: Grasshopper vehicle 32 m (106 ft, '10 stories'); lattice tower at the later stand ~25-30 m (estimate)
facilities.look: Bare concrete square pad in open field, low concrete block wall, horizontal white tanks and white containers beside the access road; a dark lattice tower and tank farm to the north-east (2020).

facilities.name: Raptor assembly building (engine factory, 2021)
facilities.function: Raptor 2 engine assembly plant announced July 2021; TDLR TABS2022002603 'SpaceX- Raptor Assembly Building', 52,000 ft2, new construction factory + limited office, Oct-Dec 2021, design Ware Malcomb.

footprint.how_known: OSM ring 1531097407 (4852 m2 = 52,200 ft2, matches TDLR 52,000 ft2) + NAIP 2022 + Esri 2025

facilities.look: Long low white flat-roofed building with a row of roof vents, parking lot with striped bays at its east end, paved yard to the south (container/equipment storage).

facilities.name: Rocket Development Hangar (RDH) + 2025 expansion
facilities.function: Large hangar in the north-east part of the property (OSM building=hangar). TDLR TABS2025005557 'RDH Expansion': 22,500 ft2 addition, Dec 2024 - May 2025 (OSM way 1531097404, 2,240 m2, on its east side).
facilities.look: Large light-grey/white high-bay hangar with a lower annex on its west side; 2025: new white extension on the east; round paved pad (~25 m) to the north-east, long concrete apron east, parking strip to the west.

facilities.name: New storage building (2026, under construction)
facilities.function: TDLR TABS2026013758 'Storage Building', 128,520 ft2 (~11,900 m2), $23 M, start 2026-03-15, completion 2026-10-31. Location on the property not public; it may be the large white building near the reveal lot in Kenny's photos (demo_layout 'white_building' at (1887,837)) - unconfirmed.
facilities.look: unknown (pre-engineered metal storage building likely)

facilities.name: Large suspended test rig (2025, 'HLS rig')
facilities.function: Big scaffolded two-tower rig with a top beam and a hanging tray, assembled Aug 2025 (precursor rig May 2025); purpose unconfirmed (NSF speculates lunar-lander / low-gravity simulation). NSF: next to an earlier test area for booster transfer tubes and header tanks. Exact position not found.
facilities.height_how_known: estimate from NSF photos (several scaffold lifts, people for scale)
facilities.look: Two lattice towers joined by a top girder, surrounded by silver scaffolding; white vertical tank and white horizontal tank on the pad behind; caliche pad on a grassy field.

facilities.name: WWII Bluebonnet Ordnance Plant magazine igloos
facilities.function: Dozens of earth-covered concrete storage magazines in diagonal rows (1942-45 ordnance plant; 'explosive magazine storage, area H' on the Solid Rocket Division plan); now in fields north-west of the Raptor complex.

footprint.area: rows across x -1900..-200, y 300..1400; each igloo ~8 x 12 m concrete front + grassy mound ~25 m

facilities.look: Small grey concrete headwalls with doors facing one way, grass-covered mounds behind, set in long diagonal rows with track roads.

facilities.name: McGregor Hercules substation (Oncor)
facilities.function: 69 kV / 12.5 kV industrial substation feeding the site (OSM, operator Oncor).
facilities.look: Fenced gravel yard with steel lattice gantries, transformers and insulators; power line pylons leading away.

facilities.name: Historic rocket-propellant plant (west, Hercules / Rocket Research era)
facilities.function: Cluster of large old industrial buildings, pipelines and a scrap yard ~2 km west of the stands inside the property boundary: the 'MANUFACTURING (M)' area of the Solid Rocket Division site plan (Phillips 1952-58, Astrodyne, Rocketdyne 1959-78, Hercules 1978-95). Current use not confirmed (not part of the SpaceX test areas in any source found).

footprint.how_known: OSM building rings (largest 435219644 ~35,600 m2 footprint ring, probably a compound outline) + NAIP 2022

facilities.look: Long low weathered metal and concrete process buildings joined by pipe racks, gravel yards, scrap yard; oval perimeter road around it.

roads.name: Plant Road (asphalt, 2 lanes, 40 mph, private)
roads.note: east-west spine north of the stands, x -1316..1935 at y -416..-23

roads.name: Campus caliche/asphalt loop
roads.note: oval road around the central stands and down to the offices; see mcgregor_data roads

open_questions: Position of the 2025 large suspended rig ('HLS rig'): NSF only says it is next to an earlier booster transfer-tube / header-tank test area. Check newer Esri/Google imagery (after Aug 2025).

Position of the 128,520 ft2 storage building (TDLR, Mar-Oct 2026). It may be the big white building at the reveal lot in Kenny's photos (demo_layout white_building at (1887,837)); imagery predates it.
Where the 2025 'junkyard' of 40-50 retired Raptors and the 'Raptor hangar' are (boneyard at (-29,-1374) or near the Raptor complex).
Tripod today: Jan-2020 shadow shows ~66 m incl. a structure on top; NSF said the tower was laid down in Oct 2019 and a blue tower is back in the 2021 photo. Exact current top structure unclear.
Heights other than water tower / tripod / structural stand are estimates; Raptor N/S stand heights unknown (no shadow-measurable imagery saved).
'NEW TEST SITE' (#10) on the 2015 numbered aerial: probably the S2 stand site (trench dug 2015) but the photo bearing does not fit well.
Main gate: no gatehouse seen; entrance placed where the concrete office drive leaves the south road (105,-2003). Public approach probably via FM 2671 and the N-S asphalt road at x~1800-1950.

Kenny's labelled aerials (aerial_labelled.webp / aerial_numbered.jpg, r/SpaceX user 'local', c. 2015) and aerial_test_stands.jpg: no full-resolution originals found (not on Commons; SpaceX Flickr search failed). Closest originals saved: the CC0 SpaceX aerials of 2008 and 2013.
